instruction.text: Victoria was next in line to the throne after her uncle, William IV. Drag their names to their position on the line of succession.

hint.label: Line of succession
hint.text: A line of succession tells us who the next king or queen will be.

atoms.b: William IV died in June 1837, making Victoria ((++queen knight)) at only 18 years old.
She was the first ever monarch to live in ((++Buckingham_Palace the_London_Eye)).
The time in which she was Queen is known as the ((++Victorian Tudor)) era.

feedback.finish: A monarch is a king or queen.

feedback.end: Victoria was officially crowned queen in 1838 in Westminster Abbey. The ceremony took over five hours, and her coronation ring got stuck on the wrong finger!

instruction.text: How do you think she might have felt on her coronation day?

finish.sound: Victoria wrote in her diary, “I shall ever remember this day as the proudest of my life.”

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps to find out what normal people thought about the day.

trainers.finishSound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'>Over 400,000 people came to see the new Queen. I loved the fireworks in the evening!</voice>

instruction.text: Select the two items that you think Queen Victoria wore at the ceremony.

feedback.end: Queen Victoria wore a gold robe over her dress too. You can see this robe if you visit Buckingham Palace!

instruction.text: Queen Victoria also reigned over the British Empire. You’re talking with a historian about the empire. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: It was all the places in the world controlled by ((++Britain Spain)) — like India, Canada and Australia. It was the largest empire in the world!
Queen Victoria really ruled over all these places?
Yes, she did. She even took the title of ((++Empress Plumber)) of India.
Did the British Empire treat people well?
No, the Empire hurt a lot of people. British people took over their land and often treated them very ((++badly good)).
